messages.subject: hessian & 2.6.2
parts:
I spent some time porting multi_normal_sufficient to 2.6.2. Is it
necessary to include stan headers in a particular order? Even though I
include,

#include <stan/math/rev/scal/fun/value_of.hpp>
#include <stan/math/fwd/scal/fun/value_of.hpp>

I still get this error,

/home/joshua/R/x86_64-pc-linux-gnu-library/3.1/StanHeaders/include/stan/math/prim/mat/err/check_symmetric.hpp:54:59: error: no matching function for call to ‘fabs(stan::agrad::var)’
if (!(fabs(value_of(y(m, n)) - value_of(y(n, m)))

Why doesn't the compiler pick the right version of value_of?

Thanks.

--

> > > #defines.

Unfortunately, there won't be a way to do this with macros because they never existed in the tagged versions of Stan 2.6.0 and 2.6.2.

> Conditional defines would allow people to upgrade OpenMx without
> upgrading StanHeaders and vice versa. It's not a big deal. It just makes
> things a little bit easier for people who don't eagerly track new
> releases.

Do you have a sense of the size of the user base that wouldn't be up for tracking new releases? This would have to be an intersection of Stan and OpenMX users. Although in principle this sounds ok, it may be over engineering the solution. That said, I'm ok with adding a version number macro.


Joshua, mind opening up an issue with a proposed macro or macros? We can have a focused discussion on the implementation on the issue thread.

> > > > How do I write #if macros that depend on the Stan version so my
> code
> > > > works for both 2.6.0 and 2.6.2?
>
> Unfortunately, there won't be a way to do this with macros because they
> never existed in the tagged versions of Stan 2.6.0 and 2.6.2.
Sure, no problem.

> > Conditional defines would allow people to upgrade OpenMx without
> > upgrading StanHeaders and vice versa. It's not a big deal. It just
> makes
> > things a little bit easier for people who don't eagerly track new
> > releases.
>
> Do you have a sense of the size of the user base that wouldn't be up
> for tracking new releases? This would have to be an intersection of
> Stan and OpenMX users. Although in principle this sounds ok, it may be
> over engineering the solution.

Well, maybe the bigger problem is that there is a potential CRAN race
condition. Suppose StanHeaders is upgraded first. Then OpenMx will fail
to install until it is updated. Same problem is OpenMx is upgraded
first. So both packages would need simultaneous upgrades on CRAN to
avoid the situation where OpenMx was uninstallable for a short time.

> That said, I'm ok with adding a version number macro.
>
> Joshua, mind opening up an issue with a proposed macro or macros? We
> can have a focused discussion on the implementation on the issue
> thread.
